title: The Academy's Mysteries
text: “That thing was apparently some slapdash contraption made by a future reincarnator as an assassin sent after Itsuki. It was modified into its current state, I take it.”

“I’ve heard about all that. The department members were thrilled to see the actual specimen, I say. Naturally they weren’t allowed to take it apart, so they’ve been continuing their observations from a distance, indeed.”

Apparently two more units came from the future as well, or so the intel goes. Truly impressive of Doctor, I say. Incidentally, this particular Doctor belongs to a department separate from both Doctor and Takt, if you can believe it. The type who only throws herself into things that interest her—and what wakes her up is the sight of Filolial-sama transformed into an angel. Same as me… an angel-transformation enthusiast, I say.
“Before long, everyone will likely get to work building a replica unit, I’d wager.”
Rafuemon’s six best-friend golems… Father’s words from before flash through my mind, I say. Please stop! I could swear I heard Itsuki’s voice just now, but surely that’s just my imagination!
“Eventually, it might be good to build support golems for Filolial-sama, starting with Fleon-chan and the others, indeed.”
“As expected of Chairman! What a splendid idea, I say!”
Filoko-chan has also been cooperating with Fleon-chan on various things. Though for some reason she never comes to the academy itself.
“I too intend to devote my whole life to crafting all manner of things, working toward golems that can sustain long-term activity through the support of Filolial-tan, I say.”
“Magnificent. So this is to be Doctor’s life’s work, indeed!”
“Of course, I’d also like to research how to continue triggering the kind of transformations in Filolials that Heroes bring about, indeed.”
“And while you’re at it, please also research how to drag Itsuki into the fold so Fleon-chan’s sense of justice can stay nice and active, I say.”
“Hmm… I’ll take it under consideration, indeed.”
And so on—Doctor and I kept the conversation lively right up until Yuki-chan’s race time, I say.
Some days later, I say.
“Buhya! Buhi buhi!”
“Buhhi buhhi!”

Itsuki came to the village and showed Father, me, and Ren footage as evidence—of pigs shredding my and Riska’s personal belongings and gloating vulgarly about it while chattering away. Mole tried to translate, but it wasn’t worth listening to, so I didn’t bother, I say. Apparently it was a scene of the pigs viciously badmouthing me and Riska behind our backs.
“Whoa…”
Father watched the footage with lifeless eyes.
“Women are terrifying.”
“Oh my, Big Sister finds it terrifying too.”
“What a nasty little crowd… Is this the everyday life at a school full of noble brats? Guess even they’ve got their struggles, in their own twisted way.”
Older Sister and Panda each offered their thoughts on the scene, I say.
“Doing such things out of jealousy toward a female superior to oneself—how ugly, nano.”
Rival was saying something or other, I say.
“Call it the dark side of prestige, or maybe… the true nature that surfaces once you toss ‘Hero’ into the mix as bait around here…”

“At any rate, over the course of a week we managed to bring quite a few of the nastier ones into line. The ringleaders now have marks against their records, and if they show no sign of remorse, they’ll be transferred to another school, apparently.”
“So how’s their behavior since the correction? Itsuki, Motoyasu-kun?”
“Everyone’s behaving themselves. They’re earnest in their studies too, and they come to me or the teachers to consult about their futures and how best to proceed.”

My grades remain excellent as ever, I say. Simple enough. Even the history questions were a breeze since the answers were right there in the textbook. Seems the stories about Trash are quite popular when it comes to modern history.

“Opinions were split whenever the abolition of duels or the meritocracy came up, but the instructors have started steering things so that if you want to flaunt your strength, you do it outside school grounds. Given Takt’s example, there’s hardly any pushback on that front.”
“Sounds like both Itsuki and Motoyasu-kun are doing fine, then. So, Ren, how’ve things been with you lately?”
Come to think of it, Ren’s been awfully quiet lately. Black Thunder, a.k.a. Kurotaro, has been so silent it’s almost sad, I say.
“Me? Some guy in Zeltoble wanted to interview me and ended up picking a fight instead, and now I’m stuck dealing with it.”
“Why?”

“He said he wanted to cover my cooking skills, so I made something, and he just went ‘Is this the best you’ve got?’ Then this incomprehensible guy started harassing me, printed some bizarre newspaper article, and now the whole culinary world’s furious at me. Naofumi, since the timing works out, mind coming by tomorrow?”
“Sure, I guess… but Ren, are you still running that cooking tournament thing?”

“No? Haven’t done that since. This was when I went to an exhibition of things I made during my blacksmithing training, and he practically forced an interview on me. Even after I told him mine was just an imitation piece.”
“Picking a fight with someone who’s already stepped back from all that—what’s wrong with this guy? A reincarnator, maybe?”
“That’s exactly what I’m suspecting too.”
Sounds like a real pain of a guy, I say. Wouldn’t it be simpler to just track him down and catch him?
“Perhaps I should go as well?”
“Motoyasu-kun, aren’t you supposed to be at the academy with Itsuki?”
“Imiya-san’s having a hard enough time as it is. Isn’t it about time Motoyasu-san doesn’t need to keep coming anymore?”
“True, the pigs have gotten quite a bit tamer these days, I say.”

I’d love nothing more than to keep talking passionately with Doctor and the others, but if I linger too long, my true identity might get exposed, I say. I made absolutely sure to sworn everyone to secrecy.
“Well, Motoyasu-kun does have the Filolials to look after too… maybe it’s about time to wind down the infiltration mission?”
“If we need something else for him to do, having him handle monster-clearing in the underground dungeon might be the safest bet. Apparently no matter how much you purify it, it never seems to end.”
“Motoyasu-kun’s fire-attribute, and the dungeon’s supposedly crawling with undead, so that should be a good match.”
“Understood, I say!”
“Oh, Bow Hero.”
Rival calls out to Itsuki here, I say.
“What is it?”

“Takt apparently found, from Rareldia’s memories, something that looks like a fragment needed for the Dragon Emperor’s class-up, hidden somewhere in this academy, nano. Seems there’s a hidden room around the restricted section of the library too—might as well deal with it while you’re at it, nano?”
“Couldn’t you have mentioned this a bit sooner, Gaelion-san?”
“If handled carelessly it might upset the land’s balance of power or something, so the academy in that other world gave an NG on messing with it, nano. Whether to destroy it is up to you, nano.”
Rival handed Itsuki a notebook scribbled full of notes, I say.
“One of the Seven Mysteries? Or more of a secret-room type thing?”
Father’s eyes are lighting right up, I say.

“There’s a Seven Mysteries story that cropped up recently. At night, a beautiful woman was seen walking toward the faculty quarters in the dormitory. Supposedly she’s the ghost of a woman who once had a romance with a teacher but died tragically. And apparently the rumor is that my room happens to be that very teacher’s old room.”
For some reason, Itsuki is looking straight at me, I say.
“Incidentally, the rumor started on the very day I took up my post.”
“Sounds like a classic case of mistaking dead grass for a ghost in the dark, I’d say…”
“Oh my.”
“What a hollow tale.”
“That wasn’t me, I say. Surely.”
So, Itsuki flips through Rival’s memo pad, I say.
“Gaelion-san. How do you get into this hidden room?”
“Only Takt knows how to get in—Rareldia’s memories can’t tell us that much, nano.”
“Some kind of mechanism meant only for reincarnators, maybe?”
“I know where it is, so if I just smash through, it should work out somehow… well, I’ll go ahead and deal with it.”
“Takt loves hidden rooms, nano. Did the same thing on Seven-Split Island, nano.”
“Ah, right, there was that. Elephant found it, and I opened the way through with Drill Mode, I say.”
Brings back memories, I say. I suppose that kind of mechanism exists here at the magic academy too, then.

“Well, setting aside the Seven Mysteries tale that seems to point at Motoyasu-san as the culprit… I’m not thrilled about it, but it does seem like there’s quite a bit more going on here. This academy has apparently had more than a few reincarnators pass through it.”

We might need to dig through everything thoroughly, Itsuki said, clearly itching to investigate. And so, I was tasked with cleaning up the dungeon beneath the magic academy, I say. Cleared it with room to spare, of course, I say. Made sure to thoroughly incinerate everything. So glad my game knowledge came in handy, I say.

That said, the atmosphere deep underground felt eerily similar to the one I’d sensed in the ruins of the Prado Desert. As it turned out later, apparently the ley lines here were tangled up with System Experience, and taking that thing down caused a chain reaction that gradually cleared away the impurity in the area, I say. And so, Itsuki’s teaching career got off to a smooth start, all things considered.

As for Ren’s little problem, once Father went and paid a visit, it was apparently resolved in an instant. The interview crew that had picked the fight ended up getting thoroughly thrashed instead and fled with their tails between their legs. Older Sister went along to check things out too, and it turned out the culprit wasn’t a reincarnator at all—just some food critic who’d taken things way, way too far, or something along those lines, I say.
